items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: The interviewee discusses Tom Brown's career, reputation ('rave of New York'), and actions ('wanted to be boss himself', 'caught a bunch of them up there') but does not state they worked together, were friends, or had a direct professional relationship. The mention of 'Custin Miller... was with Tom

ctx.x: Is he the little fellow that was out there that was and we recorded him? Oh. We recorded him, John. He played some of the cutest stuff on clarinet. You know, we were just playing for the fun of it and he was there. It was that old style, but I mean it was a nice style. It wasn't a corny style. Well, he had a nice style. No, he had a nice style.

And him and I was friends with Shillen, and Josh Gilbrot there too. After, after, after, uh, Custin Miller left, no, he was with Tom Brown. He was with Tom Brown. And he left, he left us, and we went to New York. And then we'd come back. And after, and after. It's a wonder Tom Brown didn't get with White, huh?
No. Well, Tom. At that time.

items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1958-09-24
items.q: Tom Brown grabbed ahold of me. After Tom Brown grabbed ahold of me... Tom came here to get me.

ctx.x: And did your father play ragtime?

Well, in them days there was what you call, it wasn't ragtime in them days. My father did. You know, it was dance fans, you know, but there wasn't no pep, you know? It was a regular, legitimate resistance, you see? Of course, they played with what was called ragtime in them days, but none of them was out there the Negroes. You see, my daddy gave it up. My daddy gave up music out when I was about ten years old, you see? You know, I'll never forget I was a young kid. First time I stood out all night, played with a…
I'm not going to be a man. I'm not going to be a man. I'm not going to be a man. I'm not going to be a man.
